goals.description: Identify the requested database change, database engine, ORM or migration tool, existing migration conventions, production data scale, and whether the change requires zero-downtime handling.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus only on gathering migration context. Determine what schema or data change is needed, which database and migration framework are in use, how migrations are organized, and whether the affected tables are large or production-critical.
goals.name: inspect migration context

goals.description: Choose the migration strategy and ordering, separating schema changes from data migrations and using expand-migrate-contract phases for renames, drops, and other zero-downtime production changes.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Plan the migration sequence before editing files. Separate DDL from DML, avoid editing deployed migrations, prefer forward-only production rollback via new migrations, and use expand/contract for unsafe renames or drops.
goals.name: plan safe migration sequence

goals.description: Generate or write migration files for schema changes using the project’s migration tool, applying safe patterns for columns, indexes, renames, drops, and constraints.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Implement only schema migration work in this goal. Use the detected tool’s normal workflow, include UP and DOWN where applicable, add new columns as nullable or with safe defaults, create indexes concurrently on existing large tables where supported, and do not mix data backfills into this migration.
goals.name: create schema migration

goals.description: Create separate data backfill or transformation migrations when needed, using batched processing and progress-safe patterns suitable for production-sized tables.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Implement only data migration or backfill work in this goal. Keep it separate from schema DDL, process large tables in batches, avoid long table-locking transactions, and provide an explicit reverse operation or mark the data migration intentionally irreversible when appropriate.
goals.name: create data migration

goals.description: Make any required application or ORM model changes to support the planned migration phases, such as dual reads/writes, generated clients, or removing column references before a later drop.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on application-side compatibility for the migration plan. For zero-downtime changes, ensure code can operate across old and new schema states, use dual writes/reads where planned, remove references before destructive drops, and regenerate ORM clients if the project requires it.
goals.name: update application compatibility

goals.description: Record how the migration can be recovered from or rolled forward, including DOWN migrations where supported and forward-fix plans for production deployments.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Document rollback and recovery for this migration. Prefer forward corrective migrations for production, but ensure migration files include DOWN sections where the tool expects them or clearly mark irreversible operations.
goals.name: document rollback plan

goals.description: Review the completed migration set against the safety checklist: UP/DOWN or irreversibility, no unsafe full-table locks, safe NOT NULL/default handling, concurrent indexes, separated schema/data changes, production-scale testing plan, and rollback documentation.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Perform the final safety review. Check the completed migrations and related code against the database migration checklist, verify tool-specific requirements such as non-transactional concurrent indexes, confirm schema and data migrations are separate, and note any tests or production-copy validation still required.
goals.name: validate migration safety
